a: On the device you already use, open Settings > Security > Phrase. It shows your 12 words and a sign-in QR code. On the new device, choose "Phrase login", then scan that QR with the camera, upload a photo of it, or type the words in. Your notes arrive within seconds.

[A free account covers 2 devices](/help/device-limit/) and Pro covers as many as you like, and two browsers on one computer count as a single device. Treat the QR exactly like the phrase it carries: show it to nobody, and never let it land in a photo library that syncs to somebody else's cloud.

pause-sync.q: Can I stop a device from syncing without signing out?
a: Yes. Open Settings > ID & Sync and press "Pause sync". That device stops sending anything to the server: notes, settings and files alike. You keep writing exactly as before, everything queues locally, and the moment you resume it all goes up.

The pause belongs to that device alone. It does not travel to your other devices and it never clears itself, because a switch that says "this device talks to nobody" must not be turned back on by anything except you. One thing keeps running on purpose: the small heartbeat that lets a removed device learn it was removed, which is how a [lost device](/help/lost-device/) still wipes itself.

wifi-only.q: Can I stop the app from uploading files over mobile data?
a: On Android, yes. Open Settings > ID & Sync and turn on "Files on wifi only". Your notes keep syncing on any connection, because text is tiny. Only images and attachments wait, and they go up the moment wifi comes back rather than sitting out the next retry.

Android is where the switch lives, because Android is the one platform whose app view reports wifi against cellular reliably, and a switch that guesses is worse than no switch. On a metered connection anywhere else, ["Pause sync"](/help/pause-sync/) does the same job with a bigger hammer and works everywhere.

clear-browser-data.q: What happens if I clear my browser data or cookies?
a: The web app keeps your notes in your browser's own storage, so clearing site data for PrivacyNotes wipes the local copy and signs you out. Everything that already synced is safe: sign in with your 12-word phrase and it comes back. Anything that had not synced yet is gone, because we never had a copy of it.

So do two things. Check that the footer says "Synced" before you clear anything, and keep your phrase in a password manager, because a cleared browser cannot ask you nicely for it. [The desktop and mobile apps](/help/platforms/) are not affected at all: [they keep their own storage](/help/data-on-disk/), which a browser cleanup never touches.

android-backup.q: Are my notes included in my Android phone backup?
a: No. The Android app keeps its data out of the phone's cloud backup, so none of it reaches Google Drive. The reason is the key, not the notes: where you chose **Trust this device**, your 12 words are held on that device to keep you signed in, and a cloud backup is no place for the key that decrypts your notes.

A new phone therefore starts empty: install the app, [sign in with your 12 words](/help/add-second-device/), and everything that synced arrives. Restore waits for that first sync, so a backup you bring is matched to what the account holds rather than added twice. What never synced lives only on the old phone, so check the footer reads "Synced" first, or carry a "PrivacyNotes backup (.zip)" from Settings > Import & Export > Export ([which backup to make](/help/backup-strategy/)).

A direct phone-to-phone transfer at setup is different: some phones move app data across, and Android gives an app no dependable way to refuse. That copy never leaves your two devices, so wipe the old phone afterwards.

print.q: Can I print a note or save it as a PDF?
a: Yes. Right-click a note, or open its share menu, and choose "Print / Save as PDF". Your system print dialog opens, so you can send it to a printer or save a PDF from there. The page renders clean on white with your formatting intact, whatever theme you use in the app.

It is generated on your device like every other [export](/help/export/), so nothing is uploaded to produce it. For several notes at once, select them and export as HTML: you get one printable page per note. [The "Doctor PDF" under Statistics](/help/doctor-pdf/) is a separate, purpose-built wellness report and needs Pro.

note-history.q: Can I get an older version of a note back?
a: Yes, with Pro. Open the note's "..." menu and choose "Note history" to browse up to 50 earlier versions, compare one with the current note, and restore it. Restoring loses nothing: the current text is saved as a version first, so you can step back and forth. Versions are encrypted on your device like the note itself.

Each version is the note as it stood before an edit: one is saved at your first edit after a pause of five minutes, one every ten minutes while you keep writing, and one before an edit that removes more than half of a note of 200 characters or more, unless the last version is less than 30 seconds old. Note history is the one Pro feature that runs through the server, which is why [the demo keeps its own local copy](/help/try-before-signup/) instead. Every tier has the [trash](/help/trash-auto-delete/) as well, which holds a deleted note for 30 days.

vault-totp.q: Can the Vault store my 2FA authenticator keys (TOTP / MFA codes)?
a: Yes. A Vault login has a "2FA code" field that accepts either a base32 secret or a whole otpauth:// link, and [a Bitwarden import carries existing keys across](/help/import/bitwarden/). The key is encrypted, saved and synced on every tier, free included. Pro turns it into the live rotating code with its countdown, so you do not need a second app open beside this one.

A password and its one-time code in the same vault means one unlocked device holds both factors, which is the trade every password manager with built-in codes makes. For most accounts the convenience wins, especially [with the app lock or a PIN in front of it](/help/locked-vs-protected/). If you would rather keep the two factors apart for your email or your bank, put those codes somewhere else and let the [vault](/help/vault/) carry the rest.

verify-download.q: How do I check that the app I downloaded is genuine?
a: Every build we ship is signed, and your operating system checks that signature before it runs anything. macOS builds are signed and notarized by Apple. Windows installers carry an Authenticode signature you can read under Properties > Digital Signatures. The Android APK is signed with our own key, which is why Android refuses any update that is not ours. The iPhone and iPad app is signed by Apple and only installs through the App Store. [The desktop apps also reject an update](/help/desktop-updates/) that is not signed with our key.

Download only from PrivacyNotes.app or from our [releases on GitHub](https://github.com/LifetimeLabsDev/PrivacyNotes.app/releases), which lists every version. The signature is the check that counts, and your system runs it for you: it is verified against a key that lives nowhere on our website, so a swapped file fails that check whatever the page beside it says.

family-sharing.q: Can my family share one account or one Pro purchase?
a: Two accounts is the answer, and starting a second one costs nothing: [each gets 2 devices and 50 MB free](/help/free-vs-pro/). An account is one 12-word phrase, and whoever holds that phrase holds everything in it: every note, every vault entry, on every device. Separate accounts is what gives each person their own private notes. Pro is bought per account.

To hand over one specific thing, send a [burn note](/help/burn-notes/) rather than your phrase. A shared household account works fine if that is genuinely what you want: keep the phrase in a shared password-manager entry, and treat anyone who has ever held it as having seen everything in it.

pro-after-leak.q: My recovery phrase leaked. Do I lose Pro?
a: Pro stays with the account you bought it on, and your recovery phrase is the only key to that account. If the phrase leaks and you move to a new vault, Pro does not move with you, and nobody can move it by hand, us included. The app says this at sign-up and again before you sign out: the 12 words are the only way in.

If you bought Pro in the last 30 days, you can get a [full refund](/help/refunds/) and buy again on the new vault. Each refund costs us payment fees, so please keep it for a real leak. The steps to move your notes and close the old vault are in [what to do when your phrase leaks](/help/phrase-compromised/). Keep the new phrase in a password manager, and type it nowhere else.

business-use.q: Can I use PrivacyNotes at work, and is there a team plan?
a: You can use it at work, and plenty of people do. It is a single-person tool by design: your own account, your own phrase, your own Pro purchase, with each person on a team holding their own key. There is no shared workspace, admin console or central billing.

Weigh that before you standardize on it. Encryption on each person's device means the notes belong to the person who wrote them, which is exactly what a journalist, a lawyer or a consultant wants, and it is why an organization that needs key escrow or audit logs runs those on a system built for them. For an individual professional, [self-custody is the strongest position available](/help/threat-model-levels/): the server holds nothing that opens the notes, so there is nothing for anyone to compel.

signup-options.q: Which sign-up option should I choose?
a: Whichever matches your threat level. There are three of them. One: sign in with Google, Apple, or GitHub, with your key stored on our server. Two: the same sign-in, with your key kept on your device only. Three: "Generate a phrase", with no email, no name and no login at all. All three keep your notes encrypted on your device, and what separates them is who holds the key and how much we learn about you.

Signing in with Google, Apple, or GitHub then asks where your key lives, starting on "Keep it simple & convenient". That option stores your phrase on our server, encrypted, so a new device can open your notes after provider sign-in and an authenticator code if 2FA is enabled. Save your phrase in case you lose the provider account, and keep your 2FA backup key if you enable two-factor sign-in. "Maximum security & privacy" keeps the phrase on your device, so the server holds nothing that opens your notes, and a new device needs your 12 words or [a QR scan from one already signed in](/help/add-second-device/).

The phrase-only route has no email or name tying the account to a person. In exchange the phrase is yours alone, so losing it with no unlocked device left means nobody can recover it for you. Settings > Account > Key custody shows your current mode and lets you change it. [A phrase account must first connect a provider](/help/connected-logins/) under Account > Accounts before choosing server custody; connecting alone does not change custody. Every mode can add a PIN or biometric lock and [optional two-factor sign-in](/help/enable-2fa/). The full comparison is in [the threat-level ladder](/help/threat-model-levels/).

storage-after-delete.q: I deleted files but my storage did not go down. Why?
a: Your space is already free. The moment the delete syncs, those bytes stop counting [against your quota](/help/storage-usage/), on the server as much as on this device. If the bar still shows the old figure, press the refresh icon beside it: that recounts from the server and leaves out everything queued for deletion. A device that was offline keeps its own last count until it catches up.

The "few days" the app mentions is about the encrypted file itself, not about your quota, and that wait is deliberate. Deleting a file from storage is permanent, with no trash to fish it back out of. A device that has not finished syncing holds an incomplete picture of your notes, so it could delete an image that another note still shows. A file therefore waits at least 24 hours, and only a device that has completed a clean sync removes it. The patience costs you nothing, because the space was credited the day you deleted.

spoiler-text.q: How do I hide spoiler text in a note?
a: Select the text and choose **Spoiler** in [the + menu of the toolbar](/help/format-bar/), or type it between two pairs of bars: `||spoiler||`. The text blurs at once. While you edit, it shows as soon as your cursor touches it and blurs again when the cursor moves on. [In a read-only note](/help/locked-vs-protected/), a click shows it.

The note list and previews show `•••` in its place, so not even the length gives it away. Search still finds the words inside a spoiler, an HTML export keeps them blurred until the reader clicks, and a printout shows them. A Markdown export keeps the bars, which other Markdown apps show as plain characters around the text. Spoilers are free.

copy-box.q: How do I make text that copies with one click?
a: Add a copy box: choose **Copy box** in [the + menu of the toolbar](/help/format-bar/), then type or paste the text inside it, such as a command, an address or a code. The button in its corner puts the whole text on your clipboard and shows **Copied** for a moment. A code block and a copy box turn into each other, so you can switch an existing block too.

Inline code copies as well. In a read-only note, a click or a tap on inline code copies it. While you edit, Cmd-click on a Mac or Ctrl-click on Windows and Linux copies it, so a plain click still places the cursor. A copy box saves as a code block with the language `copy`, which other Markdown apps show as a normal code block. Both are free.

statistics.q: What do the statistics show about my writing and trackers?
a: Open Settings > Statistics, or click the note and word count in the footer. **Overview** shows today and this week: words written, items edited and created, what is on your calendar today, your writing and check-in streaks, a grid of the last 26 weeks, the hours you tend to write in, growing tags and your next milestones. **Trackers** turns [the trackers in your journal](/help/journal/) into an overview with your average mood, [what lifts and drags your mood](/help/what-moves-mood/), your week, a card for each tracker and a calendar of your days; [a tap on a tracker opens its own page](/help/explore-next-day/). **Writing** shows words per day, your writing year, when you write, your top tags, note lengths, your longest notes and your milestones.

Everything is computed on your device. Words and writing hours count what you write on that device, so each device shows its own numbers. The charts, the streaks, the calendar, each tracker's page, the medication page, the year in pixels and both tracker downloads are free; Pro adds [the week in review](/help/week-in-review/), every finding and insight, the comparisons, [the dosage timeline](/help/dose-lens/), the **Doctor PDF** and [the AI prompt](/help/ai-prompt/).

drag-to-folder.q: Can I drag a note onto a folder or a tag?
a: Yes. Drag a note from the list onto a folder in the sidebar to move it there, or onto **Unfiled** to take it out of its folder. [Drop it on a tag](/help/tags/) to add that tag, and the note keeps the tags it already had. Tasks, bookmarks, contacts, Vault items and uploaded files in Files drag the same way. Rest a dragged item on a closed folder for a moment and it opens, so you can reach a subfolder.

To move several at once, Cmd-click on a Mac or Ctrl-click on Windows and Linux to select them, Shift-click to add a range, then drag any selected item. Dragging needs a mouse, trackpad or pen and a window wide enough to show the sidebar. On a phone, use **Move to folder** in the "..." menu instead. Tags are free, and [folders](/help/folders/) need Pro.

custom-themes.q: Can I make my own color theme?
a: Yes, with Pro. Open Settings > Design and choose **New theme**. Pick six colors (Background, Sidebar, Border, Text, Muted text and Accent) and the app suggests the rest, while the app behind the panel shows your theme as you go. A contrast check flags any text that is hard to read and offers **Fix all**. Save opens once every check passes.

The menu on each theme card has **Copy code**, which copies the theme as a short text code you can send to anyone, and **Paste theme code** adds one you received. [You pick one theme for light mode and one for dark](/help/appearance/), and **Favorite** in a card's menu puts up to three themes of each mode in the **Design** button in the footer, and the themes you make sync to all your devices. Find more on [the themes page](https://privacynotes.app/themes), where you can also submit your own. Type a theme's name, such as `frost`, in [Ninja](/help/ninja/) to switch to it, or `theme` to see them all. The Default theme is free, and every other theme needs Pro.

format-bar.q: Can I choose which buttons show in the toolbar?
a: Yes. Click the gear at the end of the toolbar, or open Settings > Toolbar. Every button has three homes: **On the bar**, **In the + menu** or **Hidden**. Drag a button to move it, or click it for its options. A hidden button still works through [its keyboard shortcut](/help/keyboard-shortcuts/) [and its Markdown](/help/markdown-syntax/), so hiding one takes nothing away.

Moving the bar to the top or the bottom is free on every account. Arranging its buttons is part of Pro: on a free account, Settings > Toolbar works as a preview you can try, and your layout is saved once you have Pro. Your arrangement follows your account to every device, and **Reset to defaults** brings the standard bar back. On a touch screen the bar is a single row that scrolls sideways, on every account, so no button is tucked away behind a second row.

ninja.q: What can I do with Ninja, the Cmd+K box?
a: Ninja opens any item, adds new ones and runs commands, all from one box. Press Cmd+K on a Mac or Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux, K for Katana (Cmd+P or Ctrl+P works too), or click **Ninja** in the sidebar or the list header. Type part of a title to find notes, tasks, events, journal entries, Vault items, bookmarks, contacts, files, settings, tags and folders. Under the titles, **In the text** shows the line inside a note that holds your words.

The first sign you type sets the mode: `+` [adds an item in plain words](/help/ninja-quick-add/), `>` runs a command, `#` lists your tags and `/` your folders, and `>>` after some text [adds it to a list you already have](/help/ninja-add-to-list/). Press Tab on a row for that item's menu, Option+Enter or Alt+Enter to open it in a tab, and Q anywhere to open the box with `+` typed. [Matching happens on your device](/help/search-local/), and Ninja is free.

ninja-quick-add.q: How do I add an event or a task by typing a sentence?
a: Press Cmd+K or Ctrl+K, type `+` and the sentence, for example `+Dentist fri 3pm 1h before`, and press Enter. Ninja reads the day, the time, a length, a repeat and an alert, and the rest becomes the title. Each part he read shows as a chip before you press Enter, so you see the result first. Press Q anywhere to open the box with `+` already typed.

Put `task`, `note` or `journal` first or last to choose the kind; with none, you get an event. `/Travel` puts it in a folder, `#school` adds a tag and `@work` files it in a space. To keep a word as text, put it in quotes (`"Friday" party`) or click its chip. See [the dates Ninja understands](/help/ninja-dates/). Ninja and the calendar are free, and [alerts ring with Pro](/help/reminders/).

ninja-dates.q: Which dates and times can I type in Ninja?
a: Ninja reads dates the way you would say them to a person. Type a date alone, such as `tomorrow` or `oct 31`, and the first row opens the calendar on that day. After `+`, the same words set the day of a new item:

- Days: `tonight`, `this saturday`, `day after tomorrow`, `in 3 days`, `oct 31`, `2026-12-24`
- Times and lengths: `noon`, `3pm`, `9-5`, `for 30m`, `for 3 days`
- Ranges: `fri to sun`, `oct 20-25`
- Repeats: `every weekday`, `every other friday`, `last friday of every month`, `every friday until dec 20`, `every monday 10 times`
- Alerts: `1h before`, `alert 1d and 1h`

A date in digits follows **Date format** in Settings > Date & Time, so `12/24` reads month first or day first as you set it. A year stays a year: `oct 31 2027` is never 8:27 PM. The date words follow the app language, and the word `add` works like `+` in English and in yours. [Ninja is free](/help/ninja/).

ninja-add-to-list.q: How do I add tasks to a list without opening it?
a: In Ninja, type the tasks, then `>>` and the list's name, and press Enter: `milk, eggs >> groc` adds two tasks to the end of your Groceries list, and you stay where you are. A few letters of the name are enough. A name no list has yet makes that list with the tasks in it. Into a note or a journal entry, the text goes in as a paragraph.

Commas split the tasks, and quotes keep a comma, so `"socks, warm", charger` makes two. A toast confirms what was added, and when that list is open, one Undo takes it back. Ninja never writes into [an item behind your PIN](/help/locked-vs-protected/), a read-only item or a Kanban board. [Tasks](/help/tasks/) and Ninja are free.

screen-capture.q: Can I hide my notes from screenshots and screen sharing?
a: Yes, in the apps for Android, iPhone and iPad, Mac and Windows. Open Settings > Security > Lock and turn on **Hide from screen capture**. Screenshots, screen recordings and screen sharing then show a blank window instead of your notes, as far as the device allows. On a phone it also hides your notes in the app switcher.

The switch is off by default, applies only to the device you turn it on for, and is free. Browsers and Linux give an app no way to block a capture, so the switch does not appear there. It works on its own and needs no app lock or PIN.

archive.q: What does Archive do, and how is it different from Trash?
a: Archive takes an item out of your lists without deleting it. Choose **Archive** in the item's "..." menu or its right-click menu, or in the selection toolbar for several items at once. Archived items leave All, their section, Pinned and the folder and tag counts, and wait in the **Archive** view at the bottom of the sidebar, which appears once something is archived. To keep them in All and in the counts, tick Archive in the **All** column of Settings > Lists. **Unarchive** in the same places brings an item back.

Trash is for things you want gone: it [deletes them for good after 30 days](/help/trash-auto-delete/) unless you turn that off. Archive never deletes anything, and archived items stay within reach, because a search in All, [the quick switcher](/help/ninja/) and note-links still find them. They sync and stay encrypted like everything else, and [they still count toward your storage](/help/storage-usage/). Archive works on every item type and is free.

footnotes.q: How do I add footnotes to a note?
a: Choose **Footnote** in [the + menu of the toolbar](/help/format-bar/). The app adds the next number at your cursor, creates an empty footnote below the text and puts your cursor in it. You can also type `[^1]` right after a word, and start a line with `[^1]: ` to write the footnote itself. A label can be a word as well as a number.

Click a number to jump to its footnote, and the back arrow or Escape takes you back to the text. On a computer, resting the pointer on a number shows the footnote in a small card. Numbers follow the order in the text, and the note saves standard Markdown footnotes, so other Markdown apps read them. An HTML export, a PDF and [a burn note](/help/burn-notes/) keep them as linked footnotes. Footnotes are free.

table-formulas.q: Can tables add up numbers, like a total or an average?
a: Yes. Type `=` in a table cell to pick a function, or write the formula yourself. The cell shows the answer instead of the text, and every answer updates the moment you change a cell it reads. Cells are named by column letter and row number, and the header counts as row 1, so your first row of data is row 2. The answers work on every account; picking from the menu is Pro.
To try everything at once, download the example note, then open Settings > Import & Export > Import, choose **Markdown files** and pick the file.
[Example note (.md)](/marketing/table-formulas-examples.md)
These are the functions, and they combine with `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` and brackets:

- `SUM`, `PRODUCT`, `AVG`, `MEDIAN`, `MIN`, `MAX` and `COUNT` work across a range, as in `=SUM(B2:B10)`
- `ABS`, `SQRT`, `SIGN`, `CEIL`, `FLOOR`, `ROUND` and `LOG` work on one value, as in `=ROUND(B7, 2)`
- `PI`, `E`, `TAU` and `PHI` are constants, and `RAND` gives a random number
- `=B7-B2` subtracts one cell from another, and `=SUM(B2:B10)*0.2` takes a percentage of a total

Click a cell that shows an answer and the formula comes back, ready to change. Your note stores the formula itself, never the result, so an export and any other Markdown app show `=SUM(B2:B10)` exactly as you wrote it.

checklists.q: Can I clear, sort or reorder a checklist?
a: Yes. The note's "..." menu has **Uncheck all items** to reuse a list, **Delete checked items** to clear the done ones, and **Sort items by status** to move checked items below the rest. Each one appears only when it would change something. Delete asks first, and Sort and Uncheck all can be undone with Cmd+Z or Ctrl+Z. The bottom of the note counts your progress, such as "3 of 6 checked".

To reorder by hand, drag the grip at the end of an item. Nested items move with it, and Escape cancels the drag. The grip shows when you hover on a computer and stays faintly visible on a touch screen. A checked item moves below the unchecked ones in its list by default; turn that off with **Move checked items down** in Settings > Lists. All of it is free.

find-in-note.q: How do I search for a word inside one note?
a: Press Cmd+F on a Mac or Ctrl+F on Windows and Linux in an open note, or click the magnifier in the top corner of a long note. Type the word, then press Enter for the next match and Shift+Enter for the previous one, while the bar counts the matches. Press the same keys again, or click the X, to close it. Find works in read-only notes too.

With Pro you can also replace: press Option+Cmd+F on a Mac or Ctrl+H on Windows and Linux, or choose **Find and replace** in the note's "..." menu. Replace one match or **All** of them at once, with **Match case** when you need it. Both bars also work in **Show markdown**, where they reach the raw text, such as a code block's language. To search all your notes instead, use the list search, which the / key focuses. [Every search runs on your device](/help/search-local/).

window-zoom.q: Can I make the whole desktop app bigger or smaller?
a: Yes, in the desktop apps for Mac, Windows and Linux. Press Cmd and the plus key on a Mac, or Ctrl and the plus key on Windows and Linux, to make the whole window bigger. The minus key makes it smaller, and 0 brings it back to normal. The same control is **App size** in Settings > Design, with steps from 80% to 200%.

App size scales everything at once: the sidebar, the list, the menus and your text. [To change only your writing](/help/appearance/), use **Text size** in Settings > Editor. App size applies to the device you set it on. In a browser, the browser's own zoom does the same job.

share-into-app.q: Can I share text or a link into PrivacyNotes from another app?
a: Yes, on iPhone, iPad and Android, as a beta. Tap the share button in any app and pick PrivacyNotes. [A web link becomes a bookmark](/help/bookmarks/) with the page title, text becomes a new note, and pictures and files go to Files. A link you already saved is shown instead of saved twice. Shared items arrive without a folder or a tag, so you sort them when it suits you.

On Android the app asks first: it lists what arrived and saves it only when you choose **Save all**, or drops it with **Discard**. On iPhone and iPad a card confirms **Saved to PrivacyNotes**. Each file follows your [upload limit](/help/attachment-limits/), and a share waits until you are signed in and the app is unlocked.

desktop-updates.q: How do I update the desktop app?
a: You do not have to. The apps for Mac and Windows and the Linux AppImage look for an update when they start and when you come back to them, at most every 12 hours, and download it in the background. A notice then says **Update available**, with **Restart** to finish and **Changelog** to see what is new.

The Linux .deb package updates through a new download: its notice offers **Download**, which opens the [downloads section](https://privacynotes.app/en#downloads), and you install the new package over the old one. A .deb that is too old to sync safely pauses sync until you do. If you installed with Scoop on Windows, run `scoop update privacynotes`, and the notice has **Copy command** for it. On a Mac, Homebrew needs no upgrade command, because the app updates itself.

session-expired.q: Why does the app say "Session expired"?
a: It means our server no longer accepts this device's sign-in, so syncing stops. A weak connection or a server outage never causes it: the app checks with the server a second time before it shows the message. Your notes are safe on this device.

Click **Sign in again**. The app first asks [whether you saved your recovery phrase](/help/lost-phrase/), because you need it, or the login you signed up with, to come back in. Notes that have not synced yet stay on the device and sync once you are signed in. The same window warns you [if any files have not finished uploading](/help/upload-failed/), because those are removed with the sign-out.

Zen mode hides everything except the note you are writing: the sidebar, the list and the footer, and the toolbar starts hidden too. Tabs you have open stay at the top. Press Cmd+Shift+F on a Mac or Ctrl+Shift+F on Windows and Linux, click **Zen** in the footer, or right-click an empty area and choose **Zen Mode**.

Press Escape, the same keys again, or **Exit Zen** at the top of the note to come back. **Show formatting toolbar** brings the toolbar back while you stay in Zen mode. Zen mode is part of Pro, and the [demo](https://try.privacynotes.app) lets you try it without an account.

date-format.q: Can I change how dates are shown?
a: Yes, in Settings > Date & Time. **Date format** offers Automatic, Day first, Month first and Year first (ISO), and **Clock** offers Automatic, 24-hour and 12-hour. Automatic follows the app's language and each device's region, and your choice applies on all your devices.

[Journal entries take their title from the date](/help/journal/), and **Journal titles** in the same place offers ready-made formats in your date format, or **Custom pattern** to build your own from tokens such as `YYYY`, `MMMM` and `ddd`, with words in square brackets kept as typed. A new pattern applies to new entries only. To put today's date into any note, press Cmd+; on a Mac or Ctrl+; on Windows and Linux, and add Shift for the time as well. All of it is free.

connected-logins.q: Can I connect more than one login to my account?
a: Yes. Open Settings > Account > Accounts and connect Google, Apple or GitHub to add a login that opens the same vault. You can connect several, even two accounts from one provider, and [your recovery phrase keeps working alongside them](/help/oauth-recovery/). Connecting or disconnecting an account leaves your notes and your encryption unchanged.

A login that already belongs to another vault cannot be connected, because vaults are never merged. **Disconnect** asks for your 12 words first. If we keep your phrase for you, the last connected account stays until you connect another one or save your phrase and [switch to self-custody](/help/threat-model-levels/). With self-custody, a new device still asks for your 12 words. Connected accounts are in beta.

calendar.q: Is there a calendar, and what shows on it?
a: Yes. Calendar in the sidebar shows every item with a date in one place: events, [journal entries](/help/journal/), notes and task lists with a date, and [the birthdays of your contacts](/help/contacts/). The list beside it is the agenda of the coming days, and the large view switches between Day, Week and Month. Click an empty day, or drag over empty hours, and Ninja opens with that day and time set, or drag an item to another day.

An event is its own kind of item: a note with a day, an end day, a time and a repeat. Type a whole line into [Ninja](/help/ninja-quick-add/) after `+`, for example `+Dentist fri 3pm 1h before`, and he reads the day, the time and [the alert for you](/help/reminders/). Type a day alone, such as `oct 31`, to open the calendar there. A note or a task list can carry a day, a time and an end day too, from the Schedule row of its "..." menu. The calendar is free.

reminders.q: Do calendar reminders work when the app is closed?
a: On a phone, yes: up to 64 alerts, up to 400 days ahead, are handed to the phone itself, so they ring while PrivacyNotes is closed; opening and unlocking the app hands over more. In the desktop app a reminder rings while the app runs, and in a browser while PrivacyNotes is open in a tab. Each device plans its reminders from the items it holds, so the server never learns a title, a time or a day.

Add an alert from the Alert row of an item's Schedule view, up to five per item, and set the defaults under Settings > Date & Time > Calendar, where "Show titles in reminders" also lives. [An item behind your PIN](/help/locked-vs-protected/) always rings as "Reminder" and the time, and so does every alert scheduled while the app lock is on. One handed over before the lock was on can keep its title until it rings. Reminders are part of Pro; [the calendar itself is free](/help/calendar/).

calendar-time-zones.q: What happens to event times when I travel to another time zone?
a: A time on the calendar stays the time you typed. An event at 15:00 shows and rings at 15:00 wherever your device is, the way a reminder in a to-do app does, because every time is kept as a local time with no time zone. [A phone schedules each alert for an exact moment](/help/reminders/), so after a time-zone change, open and unlock PrivacyNotes once in the new zone to move its alerts; while it is open and unlocked, it moves them by itself.
For a call with someone in another time zone, enter the time as it is where you are. If a daylight-saving change skips the hour of an alert, the alert rings at the first minute after the skip.

daily-check-in.q: How does the daily check-in work?
a: The check-in card sits at the top of Journals and asks "How are you today?" on a 1 to 10 scale. One tap saves your mood to today's entry, creating the entry if it does not exist yet, and then walks you through your other trackers one at a time: **Next** moves on, **Done** stops. The check-in options on the card let you [log another day](/help/log-missed-day/), skip today, [choose your trackers](/help/choose-trackers/) or hide the card. The check-in is free.

For a daily nudge, turn on "Daily check-in reminder" in Settings > Trackers > General and pick the time. It rings once a day on that device only, and stays quiet on a day you already logged a mood or skipped. In a browser it rings while PrivacyNotes is open in a tab. Days that hold only a check-in stay out of the journal list until you turn on **Show check-ins**.

choose-trackers.q: How do I turn trackers on or off?
a: Open Settings > Trackers > General. The built-in trackers sit in three groups, Mood & mind, Body & health and Lifestyle, and a tap turns one on or off. **Choose trackers** in [the check-in options](/help/daily-check-in/) opens the same switches. A tracker that is on shows as a pill on every journal entry and as a step in the check-in.

Turning a tracker off hides it from new entries; the values you already logged stay on their days. Every built-in tracker is free. Pro adds trackers you define yourself, see [custom trackers](/help/custom-trackers/).

Habits is a built-in tracker of yes or no questions, such as "Did you meditate?", sorted into habits to build and habits to watch. Each day the Habits pill asks the questions you switched on and counts how many you answered yes. Pick them in Settings > Trackers > General, under "Habit questions". Choosing from the built-in questions is free.

With Pro you can add up to 30 questions of your own in the same place. Write the question, give it a short name for the chip and the charts, mark it as a habit to build or to watch, and tap **Add habit**. Your own questions sit beside the built-in ones in the pill and [in statistics](/help/what-moves-mood/).

factors.q: What are factors in the journal?
a: Factors are your own words for what shaped a day, such as work, travel, a deadline or a migraine. Tap the ones that fit in the Factors pill of a journal entry, as many as apply. With Pro, [statistics compare your mood on the days with and without each factor](/help/what-moves-mood/). Factors themselves are free.

Manage the list in Settings > Trackers > Factors, or tap **Change these factors** in the pill. Add several at once by separating them with commas. The list holds up to 200 factors of up to 40 characters each, and a factor you remove keeps its name on the days that already hold it.

custom-trackers.q: Can I track something the app does not have built in?
a: Yes. With Pro you can create up to 20 custom trackers in Settings > Trackers > Custom. Give each one a name of up to 24 characters, an icon, a color and a type: a scale from 0 to 10, a scale from 0 to 5, a score from 0 to 100, a number, or yes or no. A preview shows the pill before you tap **Create**.

A number tracker can turn on **Remember last entry**, which starts each day from your previous value: useful for something that rarely changes, like your weight. You can pause a custom tracker and resume it later, and its history stays. Custom trackers appear [in the check-in](/help/daily-check-in/), in statistics and [in the tracker exports](/help/tracker-json-csv/) like the built-in ones.

log-missed-day.q: Can I log a day I missed?
a: Yes. [On the check-in card](/help/daily-check-in/), open the check-in options, choose **Log another day** and pick the day in the calendar. The card then asks how you were on that date, and your answers go into that day's journal entry. **Back to today** returns the card to the current day.

The calendar marks the days that already have an entry, so the gaps are easy to spot. A day you fill in later [counts in your statistics like any other day](/help/statistics/). In Journals, the calendar button next to the new-entry button starts a written entry for a past day in the same way.

add-medication.q: How do I add a medication with its dose and times?
a: Open Settings > Trackers > Medication and fill in the new medication form: a name, a strength such as 50 mg, a form (tablet, capsule, liquid, injection, inhaler, patch, drops or other) and an optional color. The form sets the medication's icon and the unit of each dose. Choose **On a schedule**, then how often: every day, chosen days of the week, or every few days.

Under "Times and amount", give each dose a time and an amount; **Add a time** adds more, up to 6 doses a day. Set a start day and an optional end day, then tap **Save**. Each dose appears as its own row in the Meds pill on every day it is due, and **Change these medications** in the pill brings you back here. Medication tracking is free.

as-needed-medication.q: Can I track a medication I take only when needed?
a: Yes. In Settings > Trackers > Medication, choose **As needed** [instead of a schedule](/help/add-medication/). The Meds pill then shows **Log a dose** for it rather than asking whether you took it. Each tap records a dose at that moment, and the doses of the day are listed by time, each with a button to remove it.

Set "At most a day" to see a running count such as "2 of 3 today". At that number the pill says "Daily limit reached" as a note, and you can still log a dose. Statistics count as-needed doses on their own and keep them out of the share of scheduled doses taken.

skip-dose.q: What happens when I skip or miss a dose?
a: Tap **Skip** on the dose in the Meds pill when you leave it out on purpose. The pill then asks why, with optional reasons: forgot, ran out, side effects, doctor's advice or other. Tapping the selected **Taken** or **Skip** again clears it.

On any day that has a journal entry, a scheduled dose you never mark counts as missed once its time has passed, or at the end of the day when it has no time. Days before your first logged dose do not count. The medication's page in Settings > Statistics > Trackers shows each day as taken, skipped or missed, and its figure counts every scheduled dose on its own, so a day with two doses and one skipped counts as one of two.

medication-reminders.q: Can PrivacyNotes remind me to take my medication?
a: Yes. Give each dose a time in Settings > Trackers > Medication and turn on **Remind me** for that medication. [The reminder rings at each dose time](/help/medication-reminder-privacy/) on the days the dose is due, and stays quiet for a dose you already marked. Medication reminders need Pro; [the daily check-in reminder stays free](/help/daily-check-in/).

The switch belongs to each device and does not sync, so turn it on on every device you want to hear it on. On a phone the reminder rings while the app is closed. In the desktop app and in a browser it rings while PrivacyNotes is open. A dose without a time, and [an as-needed medication](/help/as-needed-medication/), has no reminder.

medication-reminder-privacy.q: Does a medication reminder show the medication's name?
a: No. Every medication reminder reads "Medication reminder" and the time, whatever the medication, so a lock screen or a notification list never shows what you take. This holds even when "Show titles in reminders" is on [for your calendar items](/help/reminders/).

On a phone the reminder times are handed to the phone ahead of time so they ring while the app is closed, and those alerts carry only that text and the time. Tapping one opens the app at today's check-in, where you mark the dose.

medication-supply.q: Can the app tell me when I am running low on a medication?
a: Yes, with Pro. Enter the count you have in the **Supply** field of the medication in Settings > Trackers > Medication. Each dose you mark as taken counts down by its amount, and the medication's row shows how many are left.

When fewer than 7 days of scheduled doses remain, the Meds pill shows a line such as "Vitamin D: about 3 days left". After a refill, open the medication, enter the new count on hand and tap **Save**; counting starts again from there.

change-dose.q: How do I change a dose without losing the history?
a: Open the medication in Settings > Trackers > Medication, change the strength, the times, the amounts or the schedule, and tap **Save**. A schedule change applies from today, so past days keep the doses and times they had, and what you logged on them stays as it was.

Each strength change goes on the medication's page in Settings > Statistics > Trackers: the day-by-day grid marks it for everyone, and with Pro the **Dosage timeline** lists every change with its date and **Around each dose change** [compares your mood before and after it](/help/dose-lens/).

week-in-review.q: What is the week in review?
a: The week in review is a Pro summary of one week, near the end of Settings > Statistics > Trackers. It shows each day's mood, names your best and your hardest day, counts the days you logged a mood and the items you created, and marks what changed against the week before. The arrows step back to earlier weeks.
Under the summary sits a reflection box with a prompt such as "What made Tuesday good?". What you write there is [kept in your journal](/help/journal/) and syncs, encrypted, like the rest of it.

what-moves-mood.q: How does the app find what lifts or drags my mood?
a: Settings > Statistics > Trackers compares your mood on the days with and without each [tracker, factor, habit and emotion](/help/factors/), on the same day and on the next. The overview names what lifts your mood and what drags it down, and **What moves your mood** ranks them all, with each finding written out in plain words.

A comparison needs enough logged days on both sides before it shows, and it says how many more it needs. Each result is an average of your logged days: a lead worth testing, not proof of a cause. The top finding is free; Pro shows every row, the full table and the written insights.

explore-next-day.q: Can I see how sleep tonight affects my mood tomorrow?
a: Yes. In Settings > Statistics > Trackers, tap a tracker to open its page, then switch **Same day** to **Next day**. The page then compares your mood on the day after high or low values, so you see sleep tonight against mood tomorrow. **Compare with** measures the tracker against another outcome than mood, such as energy or focus.

A tracker's page, with its chart and its values by weekday, is free, and the mood page adds your year in pixels, one square per day, which you can save as an image. The same-day and next-day comparisons are part of Pro.

dose-lens.q: Can I see whether a dose change affected my mood?
a: Yes, with Pro. Open the medication's page from its card in Settings > Statistics > Trackers. **Around each dose change** compares your average mood in the days before each strength change with the days after it, and the **Dosage timeline** lists every change with its date.

A comparison needs enough logged days on both sides of the change, and it says how many more it needs. Mood moves for many reasons, so treat the result as something to talk through with your doctor. [The Doctor PDF carries the same comparison](/help/doctor-pdf/).

doctor-pdf.q: What is in the Doctor PDF?
a: The Doctor PDF is a printable Pro report to take to an appointment, made on your device from **Doctor PDF** in Settings > Import & Export > Trackers, for the range you pick. It holds an overview of the period, your mood day by day with a 7-day average, a row for each tracker, your mood on the days with and without each factor, and [the patterns the app found](/help/what-moves-mood/).

For each medication it lists the scheduled doses taken, such as "Vitamin D: 10 of 12 scheduled doses taken", a calendar of the days, and [every dose change with its date and your mood around it](/help/dose-lens/). The file leaves your device only when you save or send it yourself.

tracker-json-csv.q: What is the difference between the JSON and CSV tracker downloads?
a: Both are free, live in Settings > Import & Export > Trackers and cover the range you pick. **Download CSV** gives one row per day and one column per tracker, ready for a spreadsheet; a medication takes one column with the day's status: taken, skipped or missed.

**Download JSON** carries every tracker value with its date and definition, for another app or your own analysis. It is the complete record: each medication's schedule and its changes, its refills, and every dose with its time and [skip reason](/help/skip-dose/). Both files are made on your device.

ai-prompt.q: How does the tracker AI prompt work, and what does it send?
a: It sends nothing. **Show & copy AI prompt** in Settings > Import & Export > Trackers writes a summary of your trackers for the range you pick, shows it on screen and copies it to your clipboard. You paste it into the chatbot of your choice yourself. It is part of Pro.

The prompt holds your averages, your mood day by day, medication adherence and dose changes, the patterns the app found, and instructions for the chatbot: lead with the findings that matter most, keep the data apart from guesses, suggest small changes to try, and point out what is worth bringing to a doctor without diagnosing. Read it before you paste it, and remove anything you would rather keep to yourself.

tracker-privacy.q: Who can read my tracker and medication data?
a: Your tracker values live inside your journal entries and your medication list in your settings, and both are encrypted on your device and stay encrypted when they sync. Statistics, [the Doctor PDF](/help/doctor-pdf/), [the AI prompt](/help/ai-prompt/) and both downloads are computed on your device.

[With self-custody](/help/threat-model-levels/), the server holds nothing that opens them. If you signed up with Google, Apple or GitHub and chose "Keep it simple & convenient", your phrase is stored on our server under a key of ours; Settings > Account > Key custody shows your mode and lets you switch. More in [what PrivacyNotes can see](/help/what-can-you-see/).

trackers-in-backup.q: Are my trackers and medications in my backup?
a: Your journal entries are, with every value you logged on them, and so are your factors and your own habit questions. Your medication list and your custom tracker definitions are not in [the .zip or the encrypted backups](/help/backup-strategy/): they belong to your account's settings, which sync to every device you sign in on.

[To keep them in a file as well](/help/tracker-json-csv/), use **Download JSON** in Settings > Import & Export > Trackers, which holds every medication with its schedule, refills and dose history, and every custom tracker. A backup restored into a new vault brings back your entries, but the doses and custom values in them stay hidden there, because the medications and trackers they belong to are not in the backup.
